chapter: Washington in the 1930s: big bands, lessons, first jobs
title: Cutting lessons for the movies, then returning to the teacher
summary: He skips lessons for the Howard Theatre, is stopped by his father, asks to go back, and the teacher marvels at what he learned by ear.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I went to Mr. Boyd for I guess maybe four or five months. And, like all youngsters, you learn a little bit of something and you think you know something. Meanwhile, I was at home. I was playing every day, playing what he had taught me and trying to go beyond that, finding other chords and learning
other pieces. But the chords helped me to learn a lot of other pieces by myself, because apparently my ear was very good.

So after about, I guess, three or four months I'd say, I started just taking my 15 cents and going to the movies, or if I could find another dime, I would pull that and go to the Howard Theatre where I could see the movie and the band and the show. In other words, I started cutting my music lessons. So when my father began hearing this, I paid rather dearly for it, heh, for wasting the money, and he stopped me from taking lessons. So at that particular time, I didn't care anyway because I thought I knew enough to really... I was really playing way beyond my wildest dreams. I could play a couple of pieces that really sounded good, with both hands.

But as I played and listened to these other pianists, I began to realize that I needed something else. So I went back to my father with my tail between my legs and asked forgiveness, and I was really serious this time! So he said, 'Okay' and he sent me back.

Then, when I went back, my teacher was pretty much amazed at what I had learned when I wasn't with him, because he was always fascinated by things that I had learned without his teaching me. He would ask me, 'Play this,' and I would play something, and he'd say, 'Oh yeah, play that again.' And a
lot of pieces I really learned just from ear.
